A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MeTSK and the same core experiments, despite the revised title. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original cross-validation results, clinical generalization experiments, ablations, feature-importance maps, and domain-similarity analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds logistic-regression evaluations, foundation-model fine-tuning experiments, and training-convergence measurements.

M1.justification: The ST-GCN architecture, source and target heads, bi-level updates, contrastive objective, and frozen-representation pipeline remain unchanged. Newly documented implementation details and changes to downstream evaluation do not establish a revised MeTSK algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use HCP, the same ADHD/ABIDE sites, PTE, OASIS-3, TaoWu, and Neurocon. Additional-site experiments already appear in v1 Appendix A.2 and are retained in v2 Appendix A.5. Alternative atlases and multiclass tasks are proposed only as future work.

E2.justification: Table 2 and Figure 4 replace MLP with logistic regression, although MLP remains in other comparisons. v2 Table 7 adds fine-tuned variants of the existing Thomas et al. and BrainLM comparators. Table 5 separately contextualizes published results under different settings.

E3.justification: The reported warm-up changes from half the training steps in v1 Appendix A.3 to 20 of 90 epochs in v2 Section 5.3. Downstream probing substitutes logistic regression for MLP, and Appendix A.4 adds ADHD-Peking self-supervised fine-tuning before foundation-model evaluation. Five-fold AUC evaluation remains; these descriptions do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.3 examines optimization stability using inner-loop, self-supervised, and meta-validation loss trajectories. New Appendix A.4 tests whether adapting foundation models to ADHD-Peking changes their downstream performance. These address substantial questions about training behavior and comparison fairness beyond the retained ablations and domain-similarity analyses.

E5.justification: v2 removes Table 2's paired-t-test significance annotations and the assertion of statistically significant improvements on every dataset. It adds Wilcoxon signed-rank tests in Appendix A.2/Table 6, while Section 6.1 still describes a t-test. The statement reporting 100 stratified cross-validation iterations disappears; this establishes a reporting removal, not fewer actual runs.

E6.justification: v2 adds logistic-regression AUCs, fine-tuned foundation-model results, explicit Wilcoxon p-values, and convergence findings including 72–81% inner-loop training accuracy. For example, MeTSK's new PTE logistic-regression AUC is 0.5770, while fine-tuned BrainLM's PTE SVM AUC is 0.6102. Retained Table 2 SVM/RF results and earlier ablation/site tables are unchanged; changed classifiers do not demonstrate same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8, including the optimization objectives and domain-similarity definitions, are unchanged. The new convergence section presents empirical diagnostics rather than a theorem, proof, or mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same novelty, generalization, and scarce-data feature-extraction claims. The new conclusion largely restates existing contributions rather than changing their scientific scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations involving multisite distribution shifts and possible overfitting during foundation-model fine-tuning. It also discusses limited population coverage from small subsets and cautions against comparing literature scores obtained with different metrics, atlases, and splits. These qualify the retained interpretations without replacing them.

D1.justification: v2 adds a MeTSK code link, expanded preprocessing and connectivity-feature construction details, hyperparameter-selection descriptions, fine-tuning instructions, and computational costs, including approximately six hours on a 32-GB V100. Existing implementation material moves from Appendix A.3 to Section 5.3 and gains substantial reproducibility information.

R1.justification: New citations support linear probing, alternative atlases/connectivity measures, and the data-addition dilemma. Appendix A.1/Table 5 adds contextual comparisons with published clinical studies and explains setting differences. The central related-work narrative and novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 revises the title, edits wording and cross-references, consolidates shared preprocessing descriptions, moves implementation details into the main text, and separates Discussion and Conclusion. Most existing narrative and methodological exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds tables for literature comparisons, Wilcoxon tests, and fine-tuned foundation models, plus a three-panel convergence figure. Table 2 and Figure 4 change classifier labels and statistical annotations. Earlier appendix tables and the domain-similarity diagram are retained with relocation or renumbering, rather than newly introduced.

improvement.justification: v2 improves the evidence by testing foundation-model adaptation and training stability, and improves reproducibility through implementation details and a code link. Its comparison caveats are also useful. These gains are tempered by removal of the 100-iteration disclosure and inconsistent t-test/Wilcoxon descriptions; all newly tabulated Wilcoxon comparisons exceed p=0.05. The revision provides a limited net improvement without changing the central method or leading AUCs.
